pathway.title: PENN Entertainment, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - The retail business is stable rather than growing, and it carries the credit. Retail revenue rose 3.93% in nine months of 2026 after 0.69% in FY2025, with the Midwest and West, which hold the newly opened Joliet, Aurora and M Resort projects, up 10.27% and 9.66% while the South fell 0.75%; retail segment margin stayed between 33.01% and 33.95%. Growth is therefore development-led and the cash flow base is predictable, which suits fixed rent and interest but not a sharp fall in demand. Basis: calculation M3; calculation M4; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_pennex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 174

- The earnings recovery is real but concentrated in Interactive. Trailing Adjusted EBITDA of $1,088.2 million is 31.09% above FY2025, and the narrowing Interactive loss supplied 73.19% of the gain against 30.22% from retail, offset by higher rent expense. Interactive revenue excluding gaming-tax reimbursement fell 1.00%, so the gain came from lower costs, which creditors cannot assume will repeat. Basis: calculation M1; calculation M2; calculation M16; calculation M23; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_pennex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, pages 3–6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 42–44

- Debt-only leverage is low, but fixed lease claims make the real burden high. Net debt is 1.58x trailing Adjusted EBITDA and total debt 2.54x, yet lease and financing obligations of $8,157.6 million at present value sit outside debt, the company reports lease-adjusted leverage of 5.6x against 6.8x at the end of 2025, and cover of cash interest falls from 2.85x to 1.97x after the rent gap. Leverage tolerance should therefore be judged on the lease-adjusted basis. Basis: calculation M13; calculation M14; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-05_pennex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

- Cash generation has turned positive as development spending ended, partly through a financing choice. Free cash flow was $375.2 million in nine months of 2026 against negative $56.3 million a year earlier and capital expenditure fell to 4.59% of revenue from 8.87%, but landlord sale-leasebacks funded part of that spending, free cash flow after lease principal was $300.1 million, and the 2026 outlook of $390.0 million plus the 2028 and 2029 relocations restart the demand for capital. Basis: calculation M8; calculation M9; calculation M18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 69

- Refinancing risk is low and concentrated in one maturity. Liquidity of $2,020.9 million covers the $400.0 million of notes due January 2027 by 5.05x, only 16.90% of principal falls due by 2028 after the 2026 extensions, and refinancing the notes at the 6.75% coupon of the 2031 notes would add $4.5 million of annual interest; no rating or market price is supplied, so access is judged from the 2026 issuance at par alone. Basis: calculation M10; calculation M11; calculation M12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–19

- Governance and financial policy are the main discretionary risks. Business & governance rates governance risk medium: a $750.0 million buyback authorisation runs to 2028 after 2025 repurchases of 13.20% of opening shares, development sale-leasebacks add rent at yields of 7.73% to 7.80%, and an activist standstill ends in the 2028 cycle. None has yet reduced liquidity, but each draws on the cash flow that services debt. Basis: calculation M21; calculation M18; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32

- The primary downside path runs from retail earnings through fixed rent to cover, not through maturities. A 10% fall in trailing retail earnings, taken as an assumption, would cut Adjusted EBITDA to $893.52 million, rent cover to 1.77x and cover of interest after the rent gap to 1.46x, while liquidity of $2,020.9 million would still exceed the 2027 maturities; the stress shows in ratios and covenants before it shows in liquidity. Basis: calculation M6; calculation M7; calculation M11; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

runs.text: The strengths are five. Liquidity of $2,020.9 million covers the $400.0 million of notes due January 2027 by 5.05x and the bank facilities run to 2031 and 2033, so near-term refinancing risk is low. Trailing Adjusted EBITDA of $1,088.2 million is 31.09% above FY2025, which cuts net debt to 1.58x and lifts interest cover to 2.85x. Free cash flow of $375.2 million in nine months against negative $56.3 million shows deleveraging capacity as project spending fell. Retail segment margin stayed between 33.01% and 33.95% while revenue grew 3.93%, which makes the cash flow that pays rent and interest predictable. Debt-only measures leave a cushion: a 10% fall in trailing retail earnings, taken as an assumption, would raise net leverage only to 1.93x. Basis: calculation M1; calculation M8; calculation M3; calculation M11; calculation M13; calculation M7; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_pennex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19

The weaknesses are five. Trailing cash rent of $992.5 million, lease obligations of $8,157.6 million at present value and lease-adjusted leverage of 5.6x make fixed claims the main source of default sensitivity. Interactive lost $38.7 million in nine months and its revenue excluding tax reimbursement fell 1.00%, so 73.19% of the earnings gain rests on cost cuts. A $750.0 million buyback authorisation, after 2025 repurchases of $354.4 million, lets the board return cash from the flow that reduces debt. Four states give 42.8% of revenue and gaming taxes take 31.47% of retail revenue, so a local change moves group earnings. Covenant levels of 4.50x and 2.00x are printed without ratios or definitions, so the distance to a breach cannot be measured. Basis: calculation M13; calculation M14; calculation M2; calculation M16; calculation M21; calculation M5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: PENN completed four financing steps in 2026. On March 16 it issued $600.0 million of 6.75% senior unsecured notes due April 2031 at par, callable from April 2028, and used the proceeds to repay revolver borrowings; the issue cost $10.3 million. On April 16 the Third Amendment extended the $1,000.0 million revolver and the $446.9 million Term Loan A to April 2031 at margins of 1.50% to 2.25% over Term SOFR and removed the credit spread adjustment. In May the remaining $106.7 million of 2.75% convertible notes was repaid in cash. On May 28 the Fourth Amendment extended the $962.5 million Term Loan B to May 2033 and cut its margin by 50 bp to 2.00%. The amendments cost $16.3 million of issuance costs and a $2.4 million discount. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19

Landlord funding of development continued. Joliet ($130.0 million received August 2025, $10.1 million of added annual rent), M Resort ($150.0 million received November 2025, $11.7 million) and Aurora ($216.3 million received on June 24, 2026 against a $225.0 million sale-leaseback value, $17.4 million) were sold to GLPI and leased back, which added $39.2 million of annual rent in total. In December 2025 the Margaritaville and Greektown leases were combined into a VICI master lease with initial rent of $80.7 million, raised to $81.5 million in June 2026, and a term to May 2034. The Columbus hotel tower opened in June 2026 without landlord funding. Basis: calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49

Two relocation projects are announced. Ameristar Council Bluffs broke ground on September 14, 2026 at a cost of $180.0 million to $200.0 million for a 2028 opening, with GLPI committed to finance up to $150.0 million at a 7.1% cap rate as rent or as a five-year prepayable term loan at PENN’s option. Boomtown New Orleans will cost about $195.0 million for a 2029 opening and is expected to be financed from cash on hand, with the balance sheet and other liquidity available as alternatives. The company expects 2026 capital expenditure of $220.0 million for maintenance and $170.0 million for projects. Basis: calculation C11; calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 69

The ESPN sportsbook agreement ended on December 1, 2025 under a termination agreement of November 5, 2025. PENN paid $38.1 million in the fourth quarter of 2025 for remaining fees and $5.0 million afterwards for traditional media, the unvested part of the initial warrants was forfeited for no consideration and no bonus warrants were issued. Three warrant tranches covering 5.93% of shares outstanding remain with ESPN. The U.S. sportsbook was rebranded theScore Bet on December 1, 2025. Basis: calculation C14; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 156–157; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15

Shareholder transactions were two buybacks and one authorisation. In 2025 the company repurchased 13.20% of its opening share count for $354.4 million at an average of $17.64 per share and bought back $223.8 million of convertible notes in June 2025 at a loss of $11.8 million; no shares were repurchased in the first nine months of 2026. A new $750.0 million authorisation, approved on October 30, 2025, runs from January 2026 to the end of 2028. Basis: calculation C13; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19

The only acquisition-related exposure in the supplied documents is legacy. PENN sold Barstool to its founder in August 2023 for nominal cash and recorded a tax indemnity liability of $38.7 million at September 30, 2026, against $39.5 million at year-end 2025; the maximum future payment is not estimable. No business acquisition completed in 2025 or 2026 is described in the supplied documents. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16

fields.value: PENN Entertainment, Inc. (issuer id penn), credit snapshot pathway, as of 2026-11-05. This answer extracts and normalises the consolidated statements, debt, liquidity and leverage figures from the supplied filings and releases; it gives no recommendation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PENN’s net debt is 1.58x LTM adjusted EBITDA on carrying values, but lease and financing obligations outside that debt lift the company’s own lease-adjusted leverage to 5.6x, so creditors should read leverage on the wider basis.

fields.name: Quote

fields.value: Reported EBITDA, which carries impairment losses, gives net leverage of 2.12x, and FY2025 reported EBITDA is negative because USD 945.3 million of impairment sits inside it, so adjusted EBITDA is the usable measure for that year. Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 2.85x on the trailing twelve months but only 1.97x after the cash rent that exceeds the rent expense in EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation R14; calculation R18; calculation X4; calculation X2; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 106–107; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_pennex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is USD 2,020.9 million against USD 400.0 million of senior notes due January 2027, and covenant headroom cannot be calculated because the credit agreement is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has fallen on earnings growth and cash build rather than debt paydown. Total debt over adjusted EBITDA moved from 4.12x at the 2024 year end to 3.48x at the 2025 year end and 2.54x on the trailing twelve months, and net debt over adjusted EBITDA from 3.07x to 2.65x and 1.58x, while carrying-value debt stayed near USD 2.8 billion and cash rose from USD 706.6 million to USD 1,044.8 million. Creditors therefore depend on adjusted EBITDA holding at about USD 1,088.2 million, and the Interactive segment, whose nine-month segment loss narrowed from USD 227.6 million to USD 38.7 million, is the largest single source of earnings change.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation R4; calculation R10; calculation R16; calculation R5; calculation R11; calculation R17; calculation L3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Coverage is thinner than the headline suggests. Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 1.62x in FY2024, 2.17x in FY2025 and 2.85x on the trailing twelve months, while reported EBITDA covers 1.22x, a negative multiple in FY2025 and 2.12x. Cash rent to the REIT landlords of USD 992.5 million exceeds the USD 656.2 million of rent expense inside EBITDA by USD 336.3 million, so after that gap cover is 1.97x. A fall in earnings therefore reaches interest and lease payments together, which are largely fixed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation R6; calculation R12; calculation R18; calculation X1; calculation X2; calculation X4; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_pennex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow quality improved as development spending ended. Operating cash flow was USD 626.4 million in the nine months of 2026 against capital expenditure of USD 251.2 million, free cash flow of USD 375.2 million against negative USD 56.3 million a year earlier. Part of earlier development spending was financed by sale-and-leaseback proceeds from the REIT landlords (USD 216.3 million in 2026), which converts capex into financing obligations and rent; after principal payments on finance leases and financing obligations free cash flow for the nine months is USD 300.1 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F3; calculation F4; calculation F5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for near-term maturities. Cash of USD 1,044.8 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 976.1 million give USD 2,020.9 million, against the only large maturity inside twelve months, USD 400.0 million of senior unsecured notes due January 2027, plus current amortisation of USD 33.1 million. The revolver and Term Loan A were extended to 2031 in April 2026 and the Term Loan B to 2033 in May 2026, so the 2027 notes are the near-term refinancing event; the sources show an intent to refinance but no executed refinancing.

fields.value: Data quality and definition risks are material to how the figures are read. Reported EBITDA is derived and includes impairment losses, the issuer measures leverage three different ways, carrying-value debt differs from the issuer’s principal-based net debt by USD 38.3 million, and cash interest appears as USD 291.6 million in the cash flow statement but USD 100.9 million in the release for the nine months of 2026. Interim figures are unaudited. Each is logged with both figures, and none is reconciled silently.

fields.value: Customer-related liabilities form a non-debt funding float that the cash balance partly backs. At the 2025 year end accrued liabilities included advanced deposits of USD 75.3 million (USD 90.0 million a year earlier), unpaid wagers of USD 52.4 million (USD 56.5 million), progressive jackpot liabilities of USD 79.1 million (USD 63.3 million) and the loyalty point obligation of USD 29.8 million (USD 29.7 million), together USD 236.6 million (USD 239.5 million). Some of the cash shown in net debt is therefore owed to customers, so net debt flatters the free cash position; the breakdown is not printed at the 2026 quarter ends.

fields.value: The most material gaps are the credit agreement, which blocks covenant headroom, and the lease and financing obligations of USD 8,157.6 million at present value, which sit outside Total Debt and explain why the lease-adjusted ratio is far above the debt-only ratios. The remaining gaps limit instrument-level detail rather than the main conclusions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The covenant leverage and interest coverage ratios cannot be calculated or tested: the credit agreement’s definitions are not supplied and the filings print only the covenant levels and a compliance statement. This restricts any statement of covenant headroom. Severity: High. Action: obtain the credit agreement with its amendments and the latest compliance certificate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Lease, finance lease and financing obligations of USD 8,157.6 million at present value are separate balance sheet lines and are excluded from Total Debt, so every debt-only ratio in this analysis understates the fixed-claim burden; the issuer’s lease-adjusted ratio of 5.6x and its cash rent payments are the bridge. Severity: High. Action: carry a lease-adjusted view beside the debt-only ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - EBITDA (Reported) is not stated by the issuer and is derived as operating income plus depreciation and amortization, so it includes impairment losses (USD 945.3 million in FY2025); reported leverage is not calculable for FY2025 and the reported measure for 9M 2025 and FY2025 is negative. Severity: Medium. Action: use the adjusted ratios for FY2025 and show both measures with their labels.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Carrying values per debt instrument and scheduled amortisation per instrument are not disclosed, so instruments are shown at principal with one aggregate financing cost adjustment of USD 38.3 million; the rank of the credit facilities against the notes is not stated and the debt stack follows the stated security; the revolver carries no balance (the table prints a dash) and is left out of the stack; other long-term obligations of USD 7.8 million are left out of the stack because no rank, security or maturity is stated. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PENN Entertainment, Inc. (issuer id penn), credit snapshot pathway, as of 2026-11-05. This answer sets out the business, ownership, governance, transaction and operating facts that matter to creditors, taken from the seven supplied SEC documents and the earlier source readiness output; it draws no valuation, ranking or recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance risk is medium for PENN creditors: no controlling holder is disclosed and no liability management is documented, but $992.5 million of trailing cash rent, a $750.0 million buyback authorisation and an activist settlement running to 2028 leave creditors reliant on board restraint.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 64–65

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Retail casinos produced 81.32% of 2025 revenue and their segment earnings covered trailing cash rent only 1.96x, while Interactive still lost $38.7 million of Adjusted EBITDAR in nine months of 2026. Projects financed by landlord sale-leasebacks carry rent yields of 7.73% to 7.80%, so growth capital becomes fixed rent rather than debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; calculation C9; calculation C10; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_pennex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The business is a retail casino portfolio that depends on landlords, and that dependence is the largest creditor exposure. The four retail segments produced 81.32% of 2025 revenue and 80.62% of nine-month 2026 revenue, most of their real estate is leased from two REIT landlords, and the credit facilities carry events of default that cross-refer to the master leases. Segment earnings before rent covered trailing cash rent of $992.5 million only 1.96x, so 50.98% of those earnings is committed to landlords before interest, tax or capital spending.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; calculation C8; calculation C9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–22; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ownership is dispersed and the live governance risk is shareholder activism, not a sponsor. An activist contested the 2025 board election, and in February 2026 the company settled with a cooperation agreement that added three directors, bound the activist to a standstill and non-disparagement until the run-up to the 2028 meeting, and ended the lawsuit with prejudice. The contest cost $22.4 million of legal and advisory fees in 2025, and the activist’s holding and the board’s independence are not stated, so creditors cannot judge how much influence over capital allocation the settlement leaves with it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Shareholder returns are the behaviour to monitor: the company bought back 13.20% of its opening share count in 2025, in a year it also drew a net $570.0 million on its revolver. The documents do not tie the buybacks to that borrowing, no shares were repurchased in the first nine months of 2026, no cash dividend has been paid since the 1994 listing, and a new $750.0 million authorisation runs to the end of 2028. The credit agreement’s restricted payment capacity is not supplied, so creditors can see willingness to return cash but not the limit on it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C13; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 64–65; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Interactive is improving through lower costs, not through revenue growth. The segment’s Adjusted EBITDAR loss narrowed by $188.9 million to $38.7 million over nine months, mainly because media and advertising spend fell $133.9 million to $101.1 million after the ESPN arrangement, which carried $212.7 million of advertising cost in 2025, ended on 1 December 2025. Reported Interactive revenue grew 16.83%, but gaming-tax reimbursement from market-access partners explains all of it: excluding the reimbursement, revenue fell 1.00% to $493.3 million. Group earnings therefore still rest on the retail segments, and Interactive still loses money at the segment earnings line.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C15; calculation C18; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_pennex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 175–176; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 42–44

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Development is financed in a way that converts capital spending into fixed rent. The three completed landlord-funded projects added $39.2 million of annual rent on $505.0 million of sale-leaseback value, at rent yields of 7.73% to 7.80%, and the Council Bluffs relocation may add up to $150.0 million more at a 7.1% cap rate, as rent or as a five-year term loan at the company’s option. The New Orleans relocation of $195.0 million is planned from cash, so the company expects to fund $225.0 million to $245.0 million of the two new projects itself. This preserves liquidity today but adds fixed claims paid from the same cash flow that services debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The retail base is concentrated geographically. Ohio, Louisiana, Missouri and Pennsylvania produced 42.8% of 2025 revenue, so a local tax, competition or weather event in one state moves group cash flow more than the footprint of 42 properties in 19 states suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2026 financing was creditor-aligned and left one near-term maturity. The company issued $600.0 million of 6.75% unsecured notes due 2031 at par and repaid the revolver with them, extended the $1,000.0 million revolver and the Term Loan A to April 2031 and the Term Loan B to May 2033 with its margin cut by 50 bp, and repaid the $106.7 million of convertible notes in cash; none of the documents describes a priming, exchange or non-pro-rata step. The $400.0 million of notes due January 2027, 14.25% of principal, are classified as long-term on the company’s stated intent and ability to refinance, so their refinancing is the next test of market access.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The unsecured notes and the bank debt sit in different positions in the group. The notes are not guaranteed by subsidiaries, while the credit facilities have guarantor parties and are collateralised by interests in owned real property; the guarantors are not named in the supplied documents, so the strength of the parent-level claim cannot be judged here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a lower risk reading is that the documents show no dividend, priming, exchange or other liability management: PENN has paid no cash dividend since its 1994 listing, repurchased no shares in the first nine months of 2026, repaid its convertible notes in cash and extended all three bank facilities without a priming or exchange step. The retail segments also improved, with segment margin rising from 33.25% to 33.76% over the nine months, and the Interactive loss is shrinking. The reading would move to low if the proxy statement showed a board majority independent of any single holder, if the credit agreement’s restricted payment limits were tight and if the company published a capital return policy tied to leverage. It would move to high if repurchases resumed under the $750.0 million authorisation while retail earnings cover of cash rent stayed near 2.00x, if development beyond the three announced projects were funded by further sale-leasebacks, if the activist standstill lapsed into a new contest, or if Interactive revenue excluding tax reimbursement kept falling while losses persisted.

fields.value: - The medium risk level assumes that no holder has blocking power over capital allocation; holder percentages and board independence are not stated, so a concentrated holding or a board majority aligned with one holder would raise the level.

fields.value: - The reading of lease dependence rests on the filings’ summaries of the master leases; the lease texts and the credit agreement are not supplied, so the thresholds at which a lease default accelerates debt and the capacity for restricted payments are not established, and the exposure could be larger than shown.

fields.value: - Segment results for 2026 are unaudited and company-defined, and Segment Adjusted EBITDAR excludes the Other category that holds corporate overhead, so the 1.96x rent cover is higher than a cover after corporate costs would be.

fields.value: - The cooperation agreement is known only from its summary, so the board seats, committee rights and standstill terms beyond that summary are not established, and the protection it gives against a new contest rests on the summary.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PENN completed four financing steps in 2026. On March 16 it issued $600.0 million of 6.75% senior unsecured notes due April 2031 at par, callable from April 2028, and used the proceeds to repay revolver borrowings; the issue cost $10.3 million. On April 16 the Third Amendment extended the $1,000.0 million revolver and the $446.9 million Term Loan A to April 2031 at margins of 1.50% to 2.25% over Term SOFR and removed the credit spread adjustment. In May the remaining $106.7 million of 2.75% convertible notes was repaid in cash. On May 28 the Fourth Amendment extended the $962.5 million Term Loan B to May 2033 and cut its margin by 50 bp to 2.00%. The amendments cost $16.3 million of issuance costs and a $2.4 million discount.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Landlord funding of development continued. Joliet ($130.0 million received August 2025, $10.1 million of added annual rent), M Resort ($150.0 million received November 2025, $11.7 million) and Aurora ($216.3 million received on June 24, 2026 against a $225.0 million sale-leaseback value, $17.4 million) were sold to GLPI and leased back, which added $39.2 million of annual rent in total. In December 2025 the Margaritaville and Greektown leases were combined into a VICI master lease with initial rent of $80.7 million, raised to $81.5 million in June 2026, and a term to May 2034. The Columbus hotel tower opened in June 2026 without landlord funding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two relocation projects are announced. Ameristar Council Bluffs broke ground on September 14, 2026 at a cost of $180.0 million to $200.0 million for a 2028 opening, with GLPI committed to finance up to $150.0 million at a 7.1% cap rate as rent or as a five-year prepayable term loan at PENN’s option. Boomtown New Orleans will cost about $195.0 million for a 2029 opening and is expected to be financed from cash on hand, with the balance sheet and other liquidity available as alternatives. The company expects 2026 capital expenditure of $220.0 million for maintenance and $170.0 million for projects.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ESPN sportsbook agreement ended on December 1, 2025 under a termination agreement of November 5, 2025. PENN paid $38.1 million in the fourth quarter of 2025 for remaining fees and $5.0 million afterwards for traditional media, the unvested part of the initial warrants was forfeited for no consideration and no bonus warrants were issued. Three warrant tranches covering 5.93% of shares outstanding remain with ESPN. The U.S. sportsbook was rebranded theScore Bet on December 1, 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder transactions were two buybacks and one authorisation. In 2025 the company repurchased 13.20% of its opening share count for $354.4 million at an average of $17.64 per share and bought back $223.8 million of convertible notes in June 2025 at a loss of $11.8 million; no shares were repurchased in the first nine months of 2026. A new $750.0 million authorisation, approved on October 30, 2025, runs from January 2026 to the end of 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only acquisition-related exposure in the supplied documents is legacy. PENN sold Barstool to its founder in August 2023 for nominal cash and recorded a tax indemnity liability of $38.7 million at September 30, 2026, against $39.5 million at year-end 2025; the maximum future payment is not estimable. No business acquisition completed in 2025 or 2026 is described in the supplied documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The risk level is driven by fixed rent owed to two landlords and by an open buyback option, because rent is paid from the same cash flow as debt service and returns to shareholders would come from it too, which implies that creditors depend on board restraint until leverage falls. Countervailing evidence is the absence of dividends, of 2026 buybacks and of any priming or exchange step, and a rising retail margin. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the credit agreement and the lease texts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PENN Entertainment, Inc. (issuer id penn), credit snapshot pathway, as of 2026-11-05. This answer synthesises the issuer's fundamental credit profile from the seven supplied SEC documents and the three earlier module outputs; it gives no rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or position size.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PENN’s credit profile is adequate but lease-constrained: debt-only leverage of 1.58x is modest, yet $992.5 million of trailing cash rent lifts the company’s lease-adjusted leverage to 5.6x, so creditors rely on retail earnings holding and on the January 2027 notes being refinanced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M13; calculation M14; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-05_pennex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity of $2,020.9 million, bank maturities extended to 2031 and 2033 and free cash flow of $375.2 million in nine months of 2026 cover the $400.0 million of notes due next January. The earnings recovery is narrow, because Interactive supplied 73.19% of the $258.1 million gain in trailing Adjusted EBITDA over FY2025 and still loses money.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M1; calculation M2; calculation M8; calculation M11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The retail business is stable rather than growing, and it carries the credit. Retail revenue rose 3.93% in nine months of 2026 after 0.69% in FY2025, with the Midwest and West, which hold the newly opened Joliet, Aurora and M Resort projects, up 10.27% and 9.66% while the South fell 0.75%; retail segment margin stayed between 33.01% and 33.95%. Growth is therefore development-led and the cash flow base is predictable, which suits fixed rent and interest but not a sharp fall in demand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M3; calculation M4; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_pennex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 174

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The earnings recovery is real but concentrated in Interactive. Trailing Adjusted EBITDA of $1,088.2 million is 31.09% above FY2025, and the narrowing Interactive loss supplied 73.19% of the gain against 30.22% from retail, offset by higher rent expense. Interactive revenue excluding gaming-tax reimbursement fell 1.00%, so the gain came from lower costs, which creditors cannot assume will repeat.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M1; calculation M2; calculation M16; calculation M23; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_pennex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, pages 3–6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 42–44

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Debt-only leverage is low, but fixed lease claims make the real burden high. Net debt is 1.58x trailing Adjusted EBITDA and total debt 2.54x, yet lease and financing obligations of $8,157.6 million at present value sit outside debt, the company reports lease-adjusted leverage of 5.6x against 6.8x at the end of 2025, and cover of cash interest falls from 2.85x to 1.97x after the rent gap. Leverage tolerance should therefore be judged on the lease-adjusted basis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M13; calculation M14; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-05_pennex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash generation has turned positive as development spending ended, partly through a financing choice. Free cash flow was $375.2 million in nine months of 2026 against negative $56.3 million a year earlier and capital expenditure fell to 4.59% of revenue from 8.87%, but landlord sale-leasebacks funded part of that spending, free cash flow after lease principal was $300.1 million, and the 2026 outlook of $390.0 million plus the 2028 and 2029 relocations restart the demand for capital.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M8; calculation M9; calculation M18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 69

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Refinancing risk is low and concentrated in one maturity. Liquidity of $2,020.9 million covers the $400.0 million of notes due January 2027 by 5.05x, only 16.90% of principal falls due by 2028 after the 2026 extensions, and refinancing the notes at the 6.75% coupon of the 2031 notes would add $4.5 million of annual interest; no rating or market price is supplied, so access is judged from the 2026 issuance at par alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M10; calculation M11; calculation M12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Governance and financial policy are the main discretionary risks. Business & governance rates governance risk medium: a $750.0 million buyback authorisation runs to 2028 after 2025 repurchases of 13.20% of opening shares, development sale-leasebacks add rent at yields of 7.73% to 7.80%, and an activist standstill ends in the 2028 cycle. None has yet reduced liquidity, but each draws on the cash flow that services debt.

fields.value: Basis: calculation M21; calculation M18; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The primary downside path runs from retail earnings through fixed rent to cover, not through maturities. A 10% fall in trailing retail earnings, taken as an assumption, would cut Adjusted EBITDA to $893.52 million, rent cover to 1.77x and cover of interest after the rent gap to 1.46x, while liquidity of $2,020.9 million would still exceed the 2027 maturities; the stress shows in ratios and covenants before it shows in liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better view is that debt-only leverage has fallen to 1.58x, free cash flow turned positive and refinancing is largely done, so on a debt-only reading PENN looks comfortable. The strongest evidence for a worse view is that the fixed-charge load is far larger than the debt: lease-adjusted leverage is 5.6x, cover of interest after the rent gap is 1.97x and Interactive supplied 73.19% of the earnings gain, so the recovery is less proven than the headline. The view would improve if retail earnings cover of cash rent rose above the 2.00x of nine months of 2026 while Interactive reached breakeven, and worsen if lease-adjusted leverage returned toward the 6.8x reported at the end of 2025, if the 2027 notes were refinanced through the revolver or at a higher coupon, or if repurchases resumed under the $750.0 million authorisation before leverage fell.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M1; calculation M2; calculation M13; calculation M15; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_pennex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31–32

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant headroom is not established: the ratio definitions sit in a credit agreement that is not supplied, so the view that leverage tolerance is adequate rests on company-defined ratios, and whether the 10% earnings fall would approach the 4.50x and 2.00x tests cannot be sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No numeric management outlook is supplied except the 2026 capital expenditure plan, so the downside is a sensitivity on trailing figures rather than a forecast, and the timing of Interactive breakeven that the cash flow view relies on is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No rating or market pricing is supplied, so refinancing capacity rests on the 2026 issuance and extensions alone, and the cost of refinancing the 2027 notes at current market levels is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Trailing figures are built from FY2025 plus nine months of 2026 less nine months of 2025, so the stand-alone fourth quarter of 2025 and any seasonal swing in working capital are not shown, which could move the trailing free cash flow reading.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash of $1,044.8 million includes customer funds whose size is printed only at the 2025 year end, so liquidity may overstate cash that is free to meet maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strengths are five. Liquidity of $2,020.9 million covers the $400.0 million of notes due January 2027 by 5.05x and the bank facilities run to 2031 and 2033, so near-term refinancing risk is low. Trailing Adjusted EBITDA of $1,088.2 million is 31.09% above FY2025, which cuts net debt to 1.58x and lifts interest cover to 2.85x. Free cash flow of $375.2 million in nine months against negative $56.3 million shows deleveraging capacity as project spending fell. Retail segment margin stayed between 33.01% and 33.95% while revenue grew 3.93%, which makes the cash flow that pays rent and interest predictable. Debt-only measures leave a cushion: a 10% fall in trailing retail earnings, taken as an assumption, would raise net leverage only to 1.93x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The weaknesses are five. Trailing cash rent of $992.5 million, lease obligations of $8,157.6 million at present value and lease-adjusted leverage of 5.6x make fixed claims the main source of default sensitivity. Interactive lost $38.7 million in nine months and its revenue excluding tax reimbursement fell 1.00%, so 73.19% of the earnings gain rests on cost cuts. A $750.0 million buyback authorisation, after 2025 repurchases of $354.4 million, lets the board return cash from the flow that reduces debt. Four states give 42.8% of revenue and gaming taxes take 31.47% of retail revenue, so a local change moves group earnings. Covenant levels of 4.50x and 2.00x are printed without ratios or definitions, so the distance to a breach cannot be measured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M13; calculation M14; calculation M2; calculation M16; calculation M21; calculation M5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PENN owns, manages or holds interests in 42 gaming and racing properties in 19 states and runs online sportsbook and iCasino businesses in the United States and Canada. The retail segments produced 81.32% of FY2025 revenue and 80.62% of nine-month 2026 revenue, and most of that revenue is cash-based slot and table gaming at mature regional casinos, which gives good cash flow visibility. Most of the real estate is leased from two REIT landlords, so a large part of that cash flow is committed to rent before debt service, and Interactive adds growth in Ontario, Alberta and U.S. iCasino without yet funding itself.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M21; calculation M14; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PENN is a widely held, Nasdaq-listed parent with no controlling holder disclosed, so no sponsor behaviour can be inferred from identity, and Business & governance rates governance risk medium. The unsecured notes carry no subsidiary guarantees, while the credit facilities have subsidiary guarantors and are collateralised by interests in owned real property and the AR PENN and 2023 master leases carry a parent guarantee and cross-default each other; creditors of the notes therefore rely on parent-level claims, and the guarantor list is not supplied. The 2025 repurchases of 13.20% of opening shares show some tolerance for returning cash, while development was financed through sale-leasebacks rather than new borrowing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M21; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is driven by visits and spend per visit at regional casinos, supported by a loyalty program whose membership is reported in the tens of millions, and by online play in Ontario, Alberta and the United States. It is discretionary, local-market dependent and exposed to substitution from online gaming, prediction markets, sweepstakes and illegal operators that the company names; revenue is largely transactional, with market access agreements with partners in six states the only contract-based stream described, and pricing power is limited to promotional reinvestment. Retail revenue grew 0.69% in FY2025 and 3.93% in nine months of 2026, with the Midwest and West up 10.27% and 9.66% on new projects, the Northeast up 2.11% and the South down 0.75%, so growth outside new projects was 2.27%. Customer concentration is not disclosed. Revenue is predictable at the portfolio level, cyclical at the local level and structurally exposed to regulation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M3; calculation M4; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_pennex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gaming taxes take 31.47% of retail revenue, compensation 17.07% and other segment items 18.45%, leaving a retail margin of 33.01% in FY2025 before rent, which is fixed. Only gaming taxes move with revenue, so a 5% fall in retail revenue, taken as an assumption, would lower retail earnings by 10.38%, and margins have so far held between 33.01% and 33.95%. In Interactive, media and advertising spend fell by $133.9 million, 56.98%, and compensation by $30.0 million between nine months of 2025 and 2026, which explains most of the narrowing loss; margins can be defended under moderate volume pressure at retail but not if Interactive must restore user acquisition spend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M3; calculation M5; calculation M6; calculation M23; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 174; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 42–44

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital expenditure was 9.30% of revenue in FY2025, with $239.3 million for maintenance and $408.4 million for projects, and 4.59% in nine months of 2026; the 2026 plan is $220.0 million for maintenance and $170.0 million for projects. Trailing free cash flow of $292.0 million is 26.83% of Adjusted EBITDA, and nine-month free cash flow after lease principal was $300.1 million. Maintenance spending includes amounts the leases require, so it is not fully discretionary, while project spending is discretionary but the 2028 and 2029 relocations will cost $225.0 million to $245.0 million that the company must fund if the landlord provides its maximum. Cash conversion is adequate and improving, but it depends on the project pipeline staying landlord-funded or paced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M8; calculation M9; calculation M18; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 88; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense in mature markets: the company says most properties operate in mature, competitive markets, and a retail margin that stays within a narrow band shows limited pricing power rather than a moat. The threat of new entrants is low at retail because licences and taxes protect incumbents, and higher online, where prediction markets and sweepstakes platforms are named competitors. Substitutes include online gaming, video gaming terminals outside casinos and illegal machines, which cap retail growth to the 2.27% seen outside new projects. Buyers face no contractual switching costs and the loyalty program is the main retention tool. Suppliers matter mainly through the landlords, whose rent rises by escalators of up to 2% a year, and through technology and media partners; the ESPN arrangement showed how a supplier can carry $212.7 million of advertising cost into one year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M4; calculation M3; calculation M25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulation and tax are material and the other factors are secondary. The company operates in 28 jurisdictions under licences that depend on the suitability of owners and holders, and gaming taxes take 31.47% of retail revenue, so a state tax rise reaches earnings before rent. The economy matters through discretionary spending, with retail revenue growth of only 0.69% in FY2025. Social and technology factors operate through the shift to online play and the competition from prediction markets; they do not by themselves change liquidity or refinancing in the next two years.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M3; calculation M5; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_penn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 174

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are the cash-generative retail base, liquidity of $2,020.9 million, bank maturities to 2031 and 2033 and debt-only leverage of 1.58x. Weaknesses are fixed rent of $992.5 million, an Interactive segment that still loses money, regional and tax concentration and covenant ratios that cannot be measured. Opportunities that could lift credit quality are an Interactive breakeven, cover of cash rent rising above 2.00x and a refinancing of the January 2027 notes that extends maturities at a coupon near 6.75%. Threats are higher state gaming taxes, prediction-market and illegal competition, a restart of buybacks before leverage falls and a refinancing of the 2027 notes through the revolver or at a higher coupon.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M11; calculation M13; calculation M14; calculation M15; calculation M12; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On business profile PENN is a mid-sized regional operator with trailing revenue of $7,282.6 million spread over many properties, but with no single property or market-share figure supplied, so scale is average and diversification is regional rather than product-based. Competitive advantage rests on licences and loyalty, not on pricing power. Cost and capex flexibility is moderate: project capital is discretionary while rent and maintenance capital are not.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M9; calculation M14; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On financial profile the supports are debt-only leverage of 1.58x, interest cover of 2.85x, free cash flow of $375.2 million in nine months and liquidity of $2,020.9 million; the constraints are lease-adjusted leverage of 5.6x, cover of 1.97x after the rent gap, a reported FY2025 EBITDA that is negative because of $945.3 million of impairment, and cash that includes customer funds equal to 34.46% of year-end 2025 cash. The trend is improving: net debt over Adjusted EBITDA moved from 3.07x at the end of 2024 to 2.65x and 1.58x. Ability to refinance is supported by the 2026 issuance at par and extensions, financial policy is mixed because buybacks and sale-leasebacks coexist with debt repayment, and the missing datapoints are the covenant ratios, the guarantor list and any rating.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M13; calculation M8; calculation M11; calculation M19; calculation M20; calculation M26; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are lower project spending, a narrowing Interactive loss and a retail margin of 33.76%, and management says it is confident of a full-year Interactive earnings target that it does not print. The headwinds are the January 2027 refinancing, known rent step-ups of $4.4 million in November 2026 and $1.4 million in November 2027 against a $3.2 million step-down in May 2026, and the 2026 capital plan of $390.0 million. The company-specific outlook is therefore supportive for coverage but not for deleveraging beyond what free cash flow delivers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M3; calculation M9; calculation M22; calculation M12; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_pennex991-q32026.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 69

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the debt ladder is light until 2029, when $433.2 million falls due including the notes of July 2029, and 83.10% of principal falls due in 2029 or later, so the maturity wall sits in 2029 to 2033 after the 2026 extensions; the AR PENN and 2023 leases end their current terms in 2033 and the VICI lease in 2034, and the relocations open in 2028 and 2029. Sector headwinds are state taxes and online substitution; the sector tailwind is online legalisation in new jurisdictions such as Alberta, which the filings do not quantify.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M24; calculation M18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_penn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a drop in regional retail demand or a state tax rise in one of the four states that give 42.8% of revenue. The first operational break is lower gaming revenue at properties where compensation and other costs do not fall, so retail earnings fall faster than revenue: a 5% revenue fall lowers earnings by 10.38%. The financial transmission follows fixed rent: with a 10% fall in trailing retail earnings, an assumption, Adjusted EBITDA drops from $1,088.2 million to $893.52 million, rent cover from 1.96x to 1.77x, net leverage rises from 1.58x to 1.93x, interest cover falls from 2.85x to 2.34x and cover after the rent gap from 1.97x to 1.46x. Liquidity of $2,020.9 million still exceeds the 2027 principal of $433.1 million, so the first consequence is on ratios and covenants, which cannot be measured, and on the terms of refinancing the January 2027 notes, not on liquidity. Management levers are lower project capital, the landlord funding of the relocations and suspending repurchases; the observable triggers are retail margin below 33.01%, trailing free cash flow below $292.0 million and any revolver drawing. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress on this scenario.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M5; calculation M6; calculation M7; calculation M11; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, PENN presents an adequate business profile supported by a cash-generative regional retail portfolio and a narrowing Interactive loss, but credit quality is constrained by fixed rent and lease obligations and by a recovery that rests on Interactive cost cuts. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because retail margins held between 33.01% and 33.95% and free cash flow turned positive. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the January 2027 notes being refinanced at a coupon near the 6.75% of the 2031 notes and on the board keeping repurchases suspended. The primary downside path is a fall in retail earnings against fixed rent, which would lift lease-adjusted leverage from 5.6x toward the 6.8x seen at the end of 2025. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, the proxy statement, lease texts and any rating. Top risk: fixed rent claims on retail earnings.
